16"""Shared Ascend kernels for the fused unary ``_foreach_*`` family. 

17 

18Every operator of this family has the same shape of work: apply one element-wise 

19function to each tensor of a list. A per-tensor loop pays one kernel launch per 

20tensor (16 launches for the benchmarked lists), which on this backend costs more 

21than the math itself, so all three entry-point shapes are served by one fused 

22kernel family here: 

23 

24* out-of-place (fresh output list) and in-place (write back into the operand) 

25 differ only in whether the ``op`` pointer equals the ``x`` pointer, so a 

26 single kernel covers both; 

27* tensors of one ``(dtype, out_dtype, numel)`` bucket are packed into one 

28 launch: up to ``_MAX_SLOTS`` tensors share the grid, each program applying the 

29 tile body to every slot through constexpr ``K`` guards, so there is no runtime 

30 slot ladder and no device metadata buffer; 

31* dense / flat-addressable tensors (including transposed views, whose storage 

32 span is exactly their element set) are traversed in flat memory order, which 

33 is both exact and coalesced; genuinely gappy views go through a rank 

34 specialized strided kernel; 

35* complex64 tensors are read as their float32 view (real/imaginary adjacent in 

36 memory), one pair per logical element, so the transcendental complex math is 

37 the generic ``flag_gems.ops._foreach_complex_math`` body rather than a second 

38 copy of it. The modulus (and therefore the complex ``rsqrt``) is written out 

39 here instead: this backend lowers libdevice ``hypot`` to the naive 

40 ``sqrt(re^2 + im^2)``, which overflows for a large but perfectly finite 

41 component; 

42* bool tensors are read/written through their ``uint8`` view. A direct 

43 ``i1 -> f32`` conversion is what made the generic executor fail to compile 

44 here (the lowering emits ``sitofp i8``), and a byte compare-select both 

45 compiles and is exact for the two allowed bool values; 

46* the in-place float forms of ``trunc`` take a dedicated one-pointer kernel 

47 (see below), which is the only operator of the family whose rounding body is 

48 cheap enough that the generic two-pointer launch was the limiter. 

49 

50Block sizing is a workload-derived class, never a physical-core constant: the 

51policy picks the largest power-of-two tile that still leaves enough programs to 

52fill the vector cores, capped by the element size (a 2-byte stream can afford 

53twice the tile of a 4-byte one inside the 192 KiB unified buffer) and, for the 

54two rounding operators, by the measured per-dtype ceiling (their bodies keep 

55more fp32 temporaries alive than a copy-like map). 

56 

57dtype policy (measured against the pinned PyTorch build, same table the generic 

58executor uses): transcendentals promote integral and bool input to float32, 

59``abs`` maps complex to real and otherwise preserves the dtype, and 

60``floor``/``round``/``trunc`` preserve the dtype and reject bool and complex. 

61""" 

62

74# ``tl.constexpr`` so the very same objects are readable from inside the 

75# ``@triton.jit`` bodies, which may not capture plain module globals. 

76OP_ABS = tl.constexpr(0) 

77OP_COSH = tl.constexpr(1) 

78OP_FLOOR = tl.constexpr(2) 

79OP_ROUND = tl.constexpr(3) 

80OP_RSQRT = tl.constexpr(4) 

81OP_SIN = tl.constexpr(5) 

82OP_SINH = tl.constexpr(6) 

83OP_TAN = tl.constexpr(7) 

84OP_TANH = tl.constexpr(8) 

85OP_TRUNC = tl.constexpr(9) 

86 

87# input kind of one tensor inside the kernel 

88KIND_FLOAT = tl.constexpr(0) # float dtype: compute in fp32, round on store 

89KIND_INT = tl.constexpr(1) # integral / bool: the function preserves the dtype 

90KIND_BOOL_SRC = tl.constexpr(2) # bool promoted to float32 

91 

92_MAX_SLOTS = 16 

93_MAX_RANK = 8 

94# A bucket whose total element count is this small is launched one tensor at a 

95# time. The fused form pays off only once the work can amortise the per-launch 

96# cost, and every distinct bucket size compiles a separate K-specialised kernel, 

97# so fusing a handful of tiny correctness-sized tensors buys nothing and costs a 

98# compile per list length. 

99_FUSE_MIN_WORK = 4096 

100 

101# ``round`` / ``trunc`` are built from these constants. 

102# 

103# libdevice's ``rint`` / ``nearbyint`` / ``round`` / ``trunc`` all exist in this 

104# backend's Python libdevice but lower to nothing (the call yields ``None`` at 

105# compile time), so the rounding has to be arithmetic. ``round`` is 

106# round-half-to-even, which is exactly what the fp32 adder does when the sum is 

107# forced to integral granularity: adding ``1.5 * 2**23`` puts the sum in 

108# ``[2**23, 2**24)``, where the mantissa step is 1, for every ``|x| <= 2**22``, 

109# and subtracting the bias recovers the rounded value. Two vector ops, against 

110# floor + parity test + three selects for the explicit rule. 

111_ROUND_BIAS = tl.constexpr(12582912.0) # 1.5 * 2**23 

112# Largest magnitude a dtype's own mantissa step of 1 starts at: every value of 

113# that dtype at or above it is integral, so ``trunc`` is the identity there and 

114# the fp -> int cast is not defined. Also comfortably inside the int32 (int64 

115# for fp64) conversion range. 

116_ROUND_KEEP = tl.constexpr(8388608.0) # 2**23, fp32 

117_ROUND_KEEP64 = tl.constexpr(4503599627370496.0) # 2**52, fp64 

118 

119_INT_DTYPES = (torch.int8, torch.uint8, torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64)

124# buffer holds with a 16-slot launch depends on both; each entry below is the 

125# largest tile that compiles at 1024x1024, which is also where the operator 

126# measures fastest. 

127_TILE_CAP = { 

128 (OP_ROUND, 2): 16384, 

129 (OP_ROUND, 4): 4096, 

130 (OP_TRUNC, 2): 8192, 

131 (OP_TRUNC, 4): 8192, 

132}

146@triton.jit 

147def _real_value(x, OP: tl.constexpr, DT: tl.constexpr): 

148 """The scalar function of ``OP`` for an fp32 block ``x``. 

149 

150 ``DT`` is the dtype of the result. Both rounding operators need it as a 

151 compile-time constant: ``round`` is exact in the two-vector-op bias form for 

152 16-bit operands but needs two selects for wider ones, and ``trunc`` picks 

153 both its guard bound and its integer width from it. 

154 """ 

155 if OP == OP_ABS: 

156 return tl.abs(x) 

157 elif OP == OP_COSH: 

158 # 0.5*(e + 1/e) with e = exp(x): one transcendental, no cancellation. 

159 e = tl.exp(x) 

160 return 0.5 * (e + 1.0 / e) 

161 elif OP == OP_FLOOR: 

162 return tl.floor(x) 

163 elif OP == OP_ROUND: 

164 if DT == tl.float16 or DT == tl.bfloat16: 

165 # An fp16 operand never exceeds 65504, and the only bf16 values the 

166 # bias form cannot round are odd integers above 2**22 -- a band 

167 # bf16 cannot represent (its mantissa step there is 2**15). So the 

168 # bare bias is exact for both, with no select at all. 

169 return (x + _ROUND_BIAS) - _ROUND_BIAS 

170 if DT == tl.float32: 

171 keep = _ROUND_KEEP 

172 else: 

173 keep = _ROUND_KEEP64 

174 # Wider operands: round |x| against the dtype's integral bound, where 

175 # the biased value stays below twice that bound over the whole range, 

176 # and restore the sign afterwards (round-half-to-even is odd-symmetric); 

177 # at or above the bound the value is already integral and passes 

178 # through. Rounding |x| rather than x is what makes one bias serve both 

179 # signs; the alternative, a sign-carrying bias, needs the same number of 

180 # selects and measures slower. 

181 a = tl.abs(x) 

182 t = (a + keep) - keep 

183 y = tl.where(x < 0.0, -t, t) 

184 return tl.where(a < keep, y, x) 

185 elif OP == OP_RSQRT: 

186 return tl.rsqrt(x) 

187 elif OP == OP_SIN: 

188 return tl.sin(x) 

189 elif OP == OP_SINH: 

190 e = tl.exp(x) 

191 return 0.5 * (e - 1.0 / e) 

192 elif OP == OP_TAN: 

193 return tl_extra_shim.tan(x) 

194 elif OP == OP_TANH: 

195 # ``1 - 2/(e^2x + 1)`` saturates to +-1 exactly; written this way so a 

196 # large input never turns inf/inf into NaN. libdevice's accurate tanh 

197 # is used because the fp32 tolerance (1.3e-6) is close to the 

198 # cancellation error of the algebraic form near zero. 

199 return tl_extra_shim.tanh(x) 

200 elif OP == OP_TRUNC: 

201 # Truncation towards zero is floor below and ceil above. 

202 if DT == tl.float16 or DT == tl.bfloat16: 

203 # 16-bit operands have native floor/ceil, so this body stays in 

204 # two-byte buffers and keeps a wide tile; the integer route would 

205 # widen to fp32 (and the 16-bit -> int32 conversion does not even 

206 # lower correctly on this backend, it returns the operand 

207 # unchanged). Folding the sign in with floor(|x|) instead measured 

208 # slower here. 

209 y = tl.where(x < 0.0, tl.ceil(x), tl.floor(x)) 

210 else: 

211 # Wider operands: the fp -> int conversion truncates towards zero by 

212 # definition, one op instead of two rounding ops plus a select. A 

213 # cast is only defined inside the integer range, so the guard keeps 

214 # the operand wherever the cast is not: at or above the magnitude 

215 # where the mantissa step reaches 1 (every value there is already 

216 # integral) and for the non-finite ones. 

217 if DT == tl.float64: 

218 keep = _ROUND_KEEP64 

219 t = x.to(tl.int64).to(tl.float64) 

220 else: 

221 keep = _ROUND_KEEP 

222 t = x.to(tl.int32).to(tl.float32) 

223 y = tl.where(tl.abs(x) < keep, t, x) 

224 return y 

225 else: 

226 # Unreachable: every operator id above has its own branch. Kept so a 

227 # future id does not silently return a wrong dtype. 

228 return x 

229

231@triton.jit 

232def _int_value(v, OP: tl.constexpr): 

233 """Dtype-preserving map for integral and bool (byte) inputs.""" 

234 if OP == OP_ABS: 

235 # ``-v`` overflows at the dtype minimum exactly like ATen's abs does. 

236 return tl.where(v < 0, -v, v) 

237 # floor / round / trunc are the identity on an integral value. 

238 return v 

239 

240 

241@triton.jit 

242def _stable_hypot(re, im): 

243 """``sqrt(re^2 + im^2)`` without overflowing a large finite component. 

244 

245 The scaled form ``big * sqrt(1 + (small/big)^2)`` keeps the squares in 

246 ``[0, 1]``, so a component near the fp32 maximum reaches the result instead 

247 of overflowing to inf. libdevice's ``hypot`` measures as the naive 

248 ``sqrt(re^2 + im^2)`` on this backend, which is why this is written out. 

249 """ 

250 a = tl.abs(re) 

251 b = tl.abs(im) 

252 big = tl.maximum(a, b) 

253 small = tl.minimum(a, b) 

254 r = tl.where(big == 0.0, 0.0, small / big) 

255 return big * tl.sqrt(1.0 + r * r) 

256 

257 

258@triton.jit 

259def _c_rsqrt(re, im): 

260 """``1/sqrt(z)`` through the half-angle square root (no squaring of |z|).""" 

261 m = _stable_hypot(re, im) 

262 a = tl.sqrt(0.5 * (m + re)) 

263 b = tl.sqrt(tl.maximum(0.5 * (m - re), 0.0)) 

264 si = tl.where(im < 0, -b, b) 

265 d = a * a + si * si 

266 return a / d, -si / d 

267 

268 

269@triton.jit 

270def _complex_pair(re, im, OP: tl.constexpr): 

271 """(real, imag) of the complex result, built from the shared bodies.""" 

272 if OP == OP_COSH: 

273 return c_cosh(re, im) 

274 elif OP == OP_SIN: 

275 return c_sin(re, im) 

276 elif OP == OP_SINH: 

277 return c_sinh(re, im) 

278 elif OP == OP_TAN: 

279 return c_tan(re, im) 

280 elif OP == OP_TANH: 

281 return c_tanh(re, im) 

282 else: # OP_RSQRT 

283 return _c_rsqrt(re, im)

291@triton.jit 

292def _flat_body( 

293 xp, 

294 op, 

295 offs, 

296 n, 

297 OP: tl.constexpr, 

298 KIND: tl.constexpr, 

299 CPLX: tl.constexpr, 

300 CAST32: tl.constexpr, 

301 IS_EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

302): 

303 """One tile of ``op[i] = f(x[i])`` in flat memory order.""" 

304 if CPLX: 

305 # Two float32 words per logical element, adjacent in memory. 

306 o2 = offs * 2 

307 if IS_EVEN: 

308 re = tl.load(xp + o2) 

309 im = tl.load(xp + o2 + 1) 

310 else: 

311 m = offs < n 

312 re = tl.load(xp + o2, mask=m) 

313 im = tl.load(xp + o2 + 1, mask=m) 

314 if OP == OP_ABS: 

315 y = _stable_hypot(re, im) 

316 if IS_EVEN: 

317 tl.store(op + offs, y) 

318 else: 

319 tl.store(op + offs, y, mask=offs < n) 

320 else: 

321 yr, yi = _complex_pair(re, im, OP) 

322 if IS_EVEN: 

323 tl.store(op + o2, yr) 

324 tl.store(op + o2 + 1, yi) 

325 else: 

326 m = offs < n 

327 tl.store(op + o2, yr, mask=m) 

328 tl.store(op + o2 + 1, yi, mask=m) 

329 else: 

330 if IS_EVEN: 

331 v = tl.load(xp + offs) 

332 else: 

333 m = offs < n 

334 v = tl.load(xp + offs, mask=m) 

335 if KIND == KIND_INT: 

336 y = _int_value(v, OP) 

337 elif KIND == KIND_BOOL_SRC: 

338 y = _real_value(tl.where(v != 0, 1.0, 0.0), OP, tl.float32) 

339 elif CAST32: 

340 y = _real_value(v.to(tl.float32), OP, op.dtype.element_ty).to( 

341 op.dtype.element_ty 

342 ) 

343 else: 

344 # ``abs``/``floor`` have native 16-bit forms; computing in the 

345 # operand dtype keeps a second fp32 temporary out of the unified 

346 # buffer, which is what lets the tile be twice as wide. 

347 y = _real_value(v, OP, op.dtype.element_ty) 

348 if IS_EVEN: 

349 tl.store(op + offs, y) 

350 else: 

351 tl.store(op + offs, y, mask=offs < n)

456# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

457# dedicated in-place trunc kernel 

458# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

459# 

460# ``_foreach_trunc_`` is the one operator of this family where the generic path 

461# leaves a large amount on the table, for two reasons that this dedicated kernel 

462# removes: 

463# 

464# * the generic launch passes the operand twice (``src`` and ``dst`` alias in 

465# place), so every slot costs two pointer arguments and the body keeps a 

466# separate store stream live; 

467# * its body computes ``trunc`` in fp32 for every dtype, which pins the tile at 

468# 8192 because the rounding bodies hold 4 full-width buffers. 

469# 

470# In place there is exactly one array per slot, and both bodies below are 

471# single-array maps, so the tile can grow instead of being pinned by a fp32 

472# temporary: 8192 is the largest tile the three-lane fp32 rounding body fits in 

473# the 192 KiB unified buffer (16384 overflows it), and the 16-bit body stays on 

474# half-width integer lanes. Measured against ``torch._foreach_trunc_`` on the 

475# 16-tensor benchmark list, this kernel scores 1.23 / 1.06 / 1.18 at 256x256 

476# (generic path: 0.82 / 0.80 / 0.82) and 0.80 / 0.49 / 0.77 at 1024x1024 

477# (generic path: 0.48 / 0.39 / 0.48) for fp16 / fp32 / bf16. 

478 

479# Dtypes this kernel serves: 2- and 4-byte floats. ``float64`` (a 8-byte lane) 

480# has no measured benefit and keeps the generic path. 

481_TRUNC_FAST_DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32) 

482 

483 

484@triton.jit 

485def _trunc_tile(xp, pid, n, EVEN: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

486 """One tile of ``xp[i] = trunc(xp[i])``, in place. 

487 

488 ``xp.dtype.element_ty`` is a compile-time constant, so a launch that mixes 

489 dtypes in one bucket still gets the right body per slot. 

490 

491 fp32: ``floor`` below zero and ``ceil`` above it. Both lower to native 

492 rounding instructions, and this three-op form measured faster than the 

493 fp -> int -> fp round trip (which needs a range guard for the values the 

494 cast is not defined for) at every size. It is also exact at ``+-inf``, 

495 NaN and ``-0.0``: the comparison is false for all three negative-signed 

496 non-numbers, and ``floor`` passes them through unchanged. 

497 

498 16-bit: ``floor`` is already ``trunc`` on ``|x|``, so the sign bit is copied 

499 back from the operand instead of paying for a second rounding op and a 

500 select. The bitcast keeps the body on half-width lanes, which is what makes 

501 this path the fastest of everything measured (``ceil``/``floor`` + 

502 select, fp32 promote, and the ``int16`` round trip all measured slower). 

503 """ 

504 offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

505 if EVEN: 

506 v = tl.load(xp + offs) 

507 else: 

508 m = offs < n 

509 v = tl.load(xp + offs, mask=m) 

510 if xp.dtype.element_ty == tl.float32: 

511 y = tl.where(v < 0.0, tl.ceil(v), tl.floor(v)) 

512 else: 

513 ib = v.to(tl.int16, bitcast=True) 

514 y = (tl.floor(tl.abs(v)).to(tl.int16, bitcast=True) | (ib & -32768)).to( 

515 xp.dtype.element_ty, bitcast=True 

516 ) 

517 if EVEN: 

518 tl.store(xp + offs, y) 

519 else: 

520 tl.store(xp + offs, y, mask=m) 

521 

522 

523@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n"]) 

524def _trunc_many_kernel( 

525 x0, 

526 x1, 

527 x2, 

528 x3, 

529 x4, 

530 x5, 

531 x6, 

532 x7, 

533 x8, 

534 x9, 

535 x10, 

536 x11, 

537 x12, 

538 x13, 

539 x14, 

540 x15, 

541 n, 

542 K: tl.constexpr, 

543 EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

544 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

545): 

546 """``K`` in-place trunc tensors of one size in a single launch. 

547 

548 One program walks the same tile of every tensor, so the pointers stay static 

549 kernel arguments (no per-slot branch chain, no pointer read out of a 

550 metadata buffer) and each slot compiles away unless ``K`` reaches it. 

551 Splitting the list over several launches, or handing each program one slot 

552 through a branch ladder, both measured slower than this serial walk. 

553 """ 

554 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

555 _trunc_tile(x0, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

556 if K > 1: 

557 _trunc_tile(x1, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

558 if K > 2: 

559 _trunc_tile(x2, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

560 if K > 3: 

561 _trunc_tile(x3, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

562 if K > 4: 

563 _trunc_tile(x4, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

564 if K > 5: 

565 _trunc_tile(x5, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

566 if K > 6: 

567 _trunc_tile(x6, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

568 if K > 7: 

569 _trunc_tile(x7, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

570 if K > 8: 

571 _trunc_tile(x8, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

572 if K > 9: 

573 _trunc_tile(x9, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

574 if K > 10: 

575 _trunc_tile(x10, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

576 if K > 11: 

577 _trunc_tile(x11, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

578 if K > 12: 

579 _trunc_tile(x12, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

580 if K > 13: 

581 _trunc_tile(x13, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

582 if K > 14: 

583 _trunc_tile(x14, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

584 if K > 15: 

585 _trunc_tile(x15, pid, n, EVEN, BLOCK) 

586 

587 

588def _trunc_plan(numel, element_size): 

589 """``(tile, num_stages)`` for the dedicated in-place trunc kernel. 

590 

591 Both entries are measured, not derived from the storage width alone: 

592 

593 * a 16-bit lane costs four bytes inside the unified buffer anyway (the 

594 vector unit widens the rounding op), so the larger tile only becomes 

595 affordable because the body keeps no fp32 temporary -- but at the biggest 

596 benchmarked size the same kernel is faster with four times as many 

597 programs (tile 4096, 256 programs) than with a 16384 tile; 

598 * the fp32 body needs three full-width lanes, which fits the buffer at 8192 

599 and overflows it at 16384; 

600 * below that, ~32 tiles per launch is the same policy the rest of the family 

601 uses, which is where 2048 / 8192 come from at 256x256 / 512x512. 

602 

603 ``num_stages`` is 2 only on the one path where it measured better (2% on 

604 both 16-bit dtypes at 1024x1024); every other size is unaffected by it. 

605 """ 

606 if element_size <= 2 and numel >= (1 << 20): 

607 return 4096, 2 

608 block = 1024 

609 while block * 2 <= 8192 and block * 32 < numel: 

610 block *= 2 

611 # The launcher caps the grid at 65535 programs; widen the tile rather than 

612 # emit a grid the runtime rejects. 

613 while (numel + block - 1) // block > 65535: 

614 block *= 2 

615 return block, 1 

616 

617 

618def _apply_trunc(tensors, numel, block, num_stages): 

619 """Launch the in-place trunc kernel over ``tensors`` (all ``numel`` long).""" 

620 even = (numel % block) == 0 

621 grid = (triton.cdiv(numel, block),) 

622 for start in range(0, len(tensors), _MAX_SLOTS): 

623 chunk = tensors[start : start + _MAX_SLOTS] 

624 k = len(chunk) 

625 args = [chunk[i] if i < k else chunk[0] for i in range(_MAX_SLOTS)] 

626 _trunc_many_kernel[grid](*args, numel, k, even, block, num_stages=num_stages) 

627 

628 

629def _trunc_fast(src, kind, cplx, inplace, op_id): 

630 """Whether a prepared operand can take the dedicated in-place kernel.""" 

631 return ( 

632 inplace 

633 and op_id == OP_TRUNC 

634 and kind == KIND_FLOAT 

635 and not cplx 

636 and src.dtype in _TRUNC_FAST_DTYPES 

637 ) 

638 

639 

640# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

641# strided kernel (gappy views) 

642# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

643 

644 

645@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n"]) 

646def _strided_kernel( 

647 xp, 

648 op, 

649 n, 

650 N0: tl.constexpr, 

651 S0: tl.constexpr, 

652 N1: tl.constexpr, 

653 S1: tl.constexpr, 

654 N2: tl.constexpr, 

655 S2: tl.constexpr, 

656 N3: tl.constexpr, 

657 S3: tl.constexpr, 

658 N4: tl.constexpr, 

659 S4: tl.constexpr, 

660 N5: tl.constexpr, 

661 S5: tl.constexpr, 

662 N6: tl.constexpr, 

663 S6: tl.constexpr, 

664 N7: tl.constexpr, 

665 S7: tl.constexpr, 

666 RANK: tl.constexpr, 

667 OP: tl.constexpr, 

668 KIND: tl.constexpr, 

669 CPLX: tl.constexpr, 

670 INPLACE: tl.constexpr, 

671 CAST32: tl.constexpr, 

672 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

673): 

674 """``op[idx] = f(x[idx])`` decoding a flat logical index into an offset. 

675 

676 ``(N?, S?)`` are the collapsed dims ordered innermost-first (smallest 

677 stride first) by the host, so the fastest varying logical coordinate is the 

678 cheapest to walk. The output is contiguous when out-of-place, so a store 

679 goes to ``idx``; in place it goes back through the same decoded offset. 

680 """ 

681 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

682 idx = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

683 rem = idx 

684 off = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.int32) 

685 if RANK > 0: 

686 off += (rem % N0) * S0 

687 rem = rem // N0 

688 if RANK > 1: 

689 off += (rem % N1) * S1 

690 rem = rem // N1 

691 if RANK > 2: 

692 off += (rem % N2) * S2 

693 rem = rem // N2 

694 if RANK > 3: 

695 off += (rem % N3) * S3 

696 rem = rem // N3 

697 if RANK > 4: 

698 off += (rem % N4) * S4 

699 rem = rem // N4 

700 if RANK > 5: 

701 off += (rem % N5) * S5 

702 rem = rem // N5 

703 if RANK > 6: 

704 off += (rem % N6) * S6 

705 rem = rem // N6 

706 if RANK > 7: 

707 off += (rem % N7) * S7 

708 rem = rem // N7 

709 mask = idx < n 

710 dst = off if INPLACE else idx 

711 if CPLX: 

712 o2 = off * 2 

713 re = tl.load(xp + o2, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

714 im = tl.load(xp + o2 + 1, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

715 if OP == OP_ABS: 

716 tl.store(op + dst, _stable_hypot(re, im), mask=mask) 

717 else: 

718 yr, yi = _complex_pair(re, im, OP) 

719 d2 = dst * 2 

720 tl.store(op + d2, yr, mask=mask) 

721 tl.store(op + d2 + 1, yi, mask=mask) 

722 else: 

723 v = tl.load(xp + off, mask=mask, other=0) 

724 if KIND == KIND_INT: 

725 y = _int_value(v, OP) 

726 elif KIND == KIND_BOOL_SRC: 

727 y = _real_value(tl.where(v != 0, 1.0, 0.0), OP, tl.float32) 

728 elif CAST32: 

729 y = _real_value(v.to(tl.float32), OP, op.dtype.element_ty).to( 

730 op.dtype.element_ty 

731 ) 

732 else: 

733 y = _real_value(v, OP, op.dtype.element_ty) 

734 tl.store(op + dst, y, mask=mask) 

735 

736 

737# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

738# host helpers 

739# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

740 

741 

742def _is_flat(t): 

743 """True when ``[data_ptr, data_ptr + numel)`` is exactly this tensor. 

744 

745 Squares all non-unit dims by ascending stride and checks the strides are 

746 exactly the running product: such a tensor occupies a contiguous block of 

747 storage slots, so walking it in flat order visits its element set once. 

748 """ 

749 if t.is_contiguous(): 

750 return True 

751 numel = t.numel() 

752 if numel <= 1: 

753 return True 

754 expected = 1 

755 for stride, size in sorted((s, z) for s, z in zip(t.stride(), t.shape) if z != 1): 

756 if stride != expected: 

757 return False 

758 expected *= size 

759 return True 

760 

761 

762def _collapse(t): 

763 """Dims sorted by ascending stride, adjacent ones merged, size-1 dropped.""" 

764 dims = [(int(z), int(s)) for z, s in zip(t.shape, t.stride()) if z != 1] 

765 if not dims: 

766 return [] 

767 dims.sort(key=lambda d: d[1]) 

768 out = [] 

769 for size, stride in dims: 

770 if out and out[-1][1] * out[-1][0] == stride: 

771 psize, pstride = out[-1] 

772 out[-1] = (psize * size, pstride) 

773 else: 

774 out.append((size, stride)) 

775 return out 

776 

777 

778def _block_for(numel, element_size, heavy, cplx=False, op_id=None): 

779 """Workload-derived tile size. 

780 

781 The policy keeps roughly 32 tiles per launch so the vector cores have enough 

782 work, while the cap bounds the unified-buffer footprint of one program: half 

783 for a 4-byte stream, a quarter for the math-heavy fp32 bodies, and a much 

784 smaller tile for the complex ones, whose bodies keep both components and two 

785 hyperbolics live (a 1024-wide complex tile measured 360 KiB of buffers 

786 against the 192 KiB available). 

787 """ 

788 if cplx: 

789 cap = 4096 if not heavy else 256 

790 elif element_size <= 2: 

791 cap = 32768 

792 elif element_size >= 8: 

793 cap = 8192 

794 else: 

795 cap = 16384 

796 if heavy and not cplx: 

797 cap = min(cap, 8192) 

798 if not cplx: 

799 cap = min(cap, _TILE_CAP.get((op_id, element_size), cap)) 

800 block = min(1024, cap) 

801 while block < cap and block * 32 < numel: 

802 block *= 2 

803 # The launcher caps the grid at 65535 programs; widen the tile rather than 

804 # emit a grid the runtime rejects. 

805 while (numel + block - 1) // block > 65535: 

806 block *= 2 

807 return block 

808 

809 

810# Ops whose body is a native vector primitive, so it can run in the operand 

811# dtype (no fp32 widening temporary) and keep the wide tile. 

812_NATIVE_DTYPE_OPS = (OP_ABS, OP_FLOOR, OP_TRUNC) 

813 

814 

815def _cast32(op_id, cplx, src): 

816 """Whether the body widens to fp32. 

817 

818 ``abs``/``floor``/``trunc`` have native 16-bit forms, and for ``trunc`` the 

819 two-byte buffers are what buy it a wide tile, so all three stay in the 

820 operand dtype; everything else (including ``round``, whose bias constant is 

821 not representable in fp16) widens. 

822 """ 

823 if cplx: 

824 return True 

825 return op_id not in _NATIVE_DTYPE_OPS 

826 

827 

828def _apply_flat(batch, outs, op_id, kind, cplx, n, block): 

829 k = len(batch) 

830 is_even = (n % block) == 0 

831 cast32 = _cast32(op_id, cplx, batch[0]) 

832 grid = (triton.cdiv(n, block),) 

833 if k == 1: 

834 _flat_one_kernel[grid]( 

835 batch[0], outs[0], n, op_id, kind, cplx, cast32, is_even, block 

836 ) 

837 return 

838 args = [] 

839 for i in range(_MAX_SLOTS): 

840 j = i if i < k else 0 

841 args.append(batch[j]) 

842 args.append(outs[j]) 

843 _flat_many_kernel[grid](*args, n, k, op_id, kind, cplx, cast32, is_even, block) 

844 

845 

846def _apply_strided(src, out, op_id, kind, cplx, inplace, heavy=True, logical=None): 

847 # ``logical`` is the tensor whose (shape, stride) describes the element 

848 # order; for complex it differs from ``src``, which is the float32 view 

849 # (two words per element, one extra trailing dim). 

850 t = logical if logical is not None else src 

851 numel = t.numel() 

852 dims = _collapse(t) 

853 if len(dims) > _MAX_RANK: 

854 raise NotImplementedError("foreach unary: unsupported tensor rank") 

855 # A stride-0 write would alias several logical elements onto one location. 

856 if inplace: 

857 for size, stride in dims: 

858 if size > 1 and stride == 0: 

859 raise RuntimeError(_OVERLAP_MSG) 

860 if torch._debug_has_internal_overlap(t) == 1: 

861 raise RuntimeError(_OVERLAP_MSG) 

862 block = _block_for(numel, t.element_size(), heavy, cplx, op_id) 

863 sizes = [1] * _MAX_RANK 

864 strides = [0] * _MAX_RANK 

865 for i, (size, stride) in enumerate(dims): 

866 # complex pairs are addressed through the float32 view, so strides are 

867 # in float32 words and the pair is adjacent (2*offset, +1). 

868 sizes[i] = size 

869 strides[i] = stride * 2 if cplx else stride 

870 grid = (triton.cdiv(numel, block),) 

871 _strided_kernel[grid]( 

872 src, 

873 out, 

874 numel, 

875 sizes[0], 

876 strides[0], 

877 sizes[1], 

878 strides[1], 

879 sizes[2], 

880 strides[2], 

881 sizes[3], 

882 strides[3], 

883 sizes[4], 

884 strides[4], 

885 sizes[5], 

886 strides[5], 

887 sizes[6], 

888 strides[6], 

889 sizes[7], 

890 strides[7], 

891 len(dims), 

892 op_id, 

893 kind, 

894 cplx, 

895 inplace, 

896 True, 

897 block, 

898 ) 

899 

900 

901def _has_alias(tensors): 

902 """True when two of the in-place operands overlap the same storage bytes.""" 

903 spans = [] 

904 for t in tensors: 

905 n = t.numel() 

906 if not n: 

907 continue 

908 span = 1 

909 for size, stride in zip(t.shape, t.stride()): 

910 span += (size - 1) * stride 

911 p = t.data_ptr() 

912 spans.append((p, p + span * t.element_size())) 

913 if len(spans) < 2: 

914 return False 

915 spans.sort() 

916 prev_end = spans[0][1] 

917 for start, end in spans[1:]: 

918 if start < prev_end: 

919 return True 

920 if end > prev_end: 

921 prev_end = end 

922 return False 

923 

924 

925# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

926# dtype policy 

927# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

928 

929 

930class _Spec: 

931 """dtype rules of one operator, mirroring the generic table.""" 

932 

933 __slots__ = ( 

934 "op", 

935 "promote", 

936 "allow_bool", 

937 "allow_int", 

938 "allow_complex", 

939 "complex_real", 

940 "heavy", 

941 ) 

942 

943 def __init__( 

944 self, 

945 op, 

946 promote=False, 

947 allow_bool=True, 

948 allow_int=True, 

949 allow_complex=False, 

950 complex_real=False, 

951 heavy=True, 

952 ): 

953 self.op = op 

954 self.promote = promote 

955 self.allow_bool = allow_bool 

956 self.allow_int = allow_int 

957 self.allow_complex = allow_complex 

958 self.complex_real = complex_real 

959 self.heavy = heavy 

960 

961 def out_dtype(self, dtype): 

962 if dtype.is_complex: 

963 if not self.allow_complex: 

964 raise RuntimeError( 

965 "not implemented for '%s'" % str(dtype).replace("torch.", "") 

966 ) 

967 return torch.float32 if self.complex_real else dtype 

968 if dtype is torch.bool: 

969 if not self.allow_bool: 

970 raise RuntimeError( 

971 "not implemented for '%s'" % str(dtype).replace("torch.", "") 

972 ) 

973 return torch.float32 if self.promote else dtype 

974 if dtype.is_floating_point: 

975 return dtype 

976 if dtype not in _INT_DTYPES: 

977 raise RuntimeError( 

978 "not implemented for '%s'" % str(dtype).replace("torch.", "") 

979 ) 

980 if not self.allow_int: 

981 raise RuntimeError( 

982 "not implemented for '%s'" % str(dtype).replace("torch.", "") 

983 ) 

984 return torch.float32 if self.promote else dtype 

985 

986 

987def _kernel_kind(dtype, out_dtype): 

988 """Which body the kernel runs for this operand. 

989 

990 An integral input that promotes to float runs the fp32 math, not the 

991 dtype-preserving map: ``int -> float32`` has to convert first. 

992 """ 

993 if dtype.is_complex or dtype.is_floating_point: 

994 return KIND_FLOAT 

995 if dtype is torch.bool: 

996 return KIND_INT if out_dtype is torch.bool else KIND_BOOL_SRC 

997 return KIND_INT if out_dtype is dtype else KIND_FLOAT 

998 

999 

1000def _prepare(t, out_dtype, flat, inplace): 

1001 """Kernel views of the operand and the result, plus kind/cplx flags. 

1002 

1003 A complex tensor is addressed through its float32 view (real/imaginary 

1004 adjacent) and a bool tensor through its uint8 view; the logical tensor is 

1005 returned separately so the caller can hand the real object back. 

1006 """ 

1007 dtype = t.dtype 

1008 cplx = dtype.is_complex 

1009 kind = _kernel_kind(dtype, out_dtype) 

1010 src = ( 

1011 t.view(torch.float32) 

1012 if cplx 

1013 else (t.view(torch.uint8) if dtype is torch.bool else t) 

1014 ) 

1015 if inplace: 

1016 return src, src, t, kind, cplx 

1017 # A flat-addressable operand is walked in storage order, so the result has 

1018 # to cover the same slots in the same order. ``empty_like`` does *not* 

1019 # preserve a non-contiguous layout on this backend (it returns a base-format 

1020 # tensor), so the strides are requested explicitly for a flat operand; a 

1021 # gappy view goes through the strided kernel in logical order instead and 

1022 # gets a plain contiguous result. 

1023 if not flat: 

1024 out = torch.empty(t.shape, dtype=out_dtype, device=t.device) 

1025 elif t.is_contiguous(): 

1026 out = torch.empty_like(t, dtype=out_dtype) 

1027 else: 

1028 out = torch.empty_strided(t.shape, t.stride(), dtype=out_dtype, device=t.device) 

1029 dst = ( 

1030 out.view(torch.float32) 

1031 if cplx 

1032 else (out.view(torch.uint8) if out_dtype is torch.bool else out) 

1033 ) 

1034 return src, dst, out, kind, cplx 

1035 

1036 

1037def _run(spec, tensors, inplace): 

1038 """Shared entry point: validate, bucket, and launch.""" 

1039 if isinstance(tensors, torch.Tensor): 

1040 raise TypeError("run() expects a sequence of Tensor, got a single Tensor") 

1041 if not isinstance(tensors, (list, tuple)): 

1042 raise TypeError("argument 'self' must be tuple of Tensors") 

1043 values = list(tensors) 

1044 if not values: 

1045 raise RuntimeError("Tensor list must have at least one tensor.") 

1046 for t in values: 

1047 if not isinstance(t, torch.Tensor): 

1048 raise TypeError("expected Tensor as element in argument 0") 

1049 

1050 # Validation and classification pass; nothing is launched until every 

1051 # element of the list has been accepted, matching ATen's all-or-nothing 

1052 # refusal. 

1053 outs = [None] * len(values) 

1054 prepared = [] # (src, dst, kind, cplx, numel, block, flat, logical) 

1055 for i, t in enumerate(values): 

1056 out_dtype = spec.out_dtype(t.dtype) 

1057 if inplace and out_dtype is not t.dtype: 

1058 if t.dtype.is_complex: 

1059 raise RuntimeError( 

1060 "In-place %s is not supported for complex tensors." 

1061 % _OP_NAMES[spec.op] 

1062 ) 

1063 raise RuntimeError( 

1064 "result type Float can't be cast to the desired output type " 

1065 + str(t.dtype).replace("torch.", "").capitalize() 

1066 ) 

1067 numel = t.numel() 

1068 flat = numel <= 1 or _is_flat(t) 

1069 src, dst, out, kind, cplx = _prepare(t, out_dtype, flat, inplace) 

1070 if not inplace: 

1071 outs[i] = out 

1072 if numel == 0 or ( 

1073 inplace and kind == KIND_INT and spec.op in (OP_FLOOR, OP_ROUND, OP_TRUNC) 

1074 ): 

1075 # An integral in-place map is the identity, so there is nothing to 

1076 # write (and no output to allocate for the functional form). 

1077 continue 

1078 block = ( 

1079 _block_for(numel, t.element_size(), spec.heavy, cplx, spec.op) 

1080 if flat 

1081 else 0 

1082 ) 

1083 prepared.append((src, dst, kind, cplx, numel, block, flat, t)) 

1084 

1085 # In-place writes to overlapping storage depend on list order; fusing 

1086 # reorders them, so an aliased list falls back to the sequential path. 

1087 if inplace and _has_alias(values): 

1088 for src, dst, kind, cplx, numel, block, flat, logical in prepared: 

1089 if flat: 

1090 if _trunc_fast(src, kind, cplx, inplace, spec.op): 

1091 block, num_stages = _trunc_plan(numel, src.element_size()) 

1092 _apply_trunc([src], numel, block, num_stages) 

1093 else: 

1094 _apply_flat([src], [dst], spec.op, kind, cplx, numel, block) 

1095 else: 

1096 _apply_strided(src, dst, spec.op, kind, cplx, True, spec.heavy, logical) 

1097 return None 

1098 

1099 buckets = {} 

1100 # In-place trunc has its own kernel and its own tile policy, so its operands 

1101 # are grouped separately from the generic buckets; mixed dtypes may share a 

1102 # launch because the body dispatches on the pointer's element type. 

1103 trunc_groups = {} 

1104 for src, dst, kind, cplx, numel, block, flat, logical in prepared: 

1105 if not flat: 

1106 _apply_strided(src, dst, spec.op, kind, cplx, inplace, spec.heavy, logical) 

1107 continue 

1108 if _trunc_fast(src, kind, cplx, inplace, spec.op): 

1109 tile, num_stages = _trunc_plan(numel, src.element_size()) 

1110 trunc_groups.setdefault((numel, tile, num_stages), []).append(src) 

1111 continue 

1112 buckets.setdefault((kind, cplx, numel, block), []).append((src, dst)) 

1113 for (numel, tile, num_stages), tensors in trunc_groups.items(): 

1114 _apply_trunc(tensors, numel, tile, num_stages) 

1115 for (kind, cplx, numel, block), items in buckets.items(): 

1116 slots = _MAX_SLOTS if numel * len(items) > _FUSE_MIN_WORK else 1 

1117 for start in range(0, len(items), slots): 

1118 chunk = items[start : start + slots] 

1119 _apply_flat( 

1120 [c[0] for c in chunk], 

1121 [c[1] for c in chunk], 

1122 spec.op, 

1123 kind, 

1124 cplx, 

1125 numel, 

1126 block, 

1127 ) 

1128 return None if inplace else outs 

1129 

1130 

1131_OP_NAMES = { 

1132 OP_ABS: "abs", 

1133 OP_COSH: "cosh", 

1134 OP_FLOOR: "floor", 

1135 OP_ROUND: "round", 

1136 OP_RSQRT: "rsqrt",
